decisions.reason: Accepting a high-MOQ connector purchase does not change the required PCB production export files.
The source changes the sourcing fallback for a connector but does not change BOM completeness, part-number requirements, or any listed BOM attribute.
Connector purchasing and minimum quantity do not affect the requirement to label connector pins on the board.
The client accepts a component-sourcing fallback but does not change how board orders are configured, placed in the cart, or conditioned on missing-part availability.
The high-MOQ purchasing decision does not alter the requirement to validate component orientations in JLCPCB.
The source concerns the connector sourcing fallback and does not revise the separately approved buzzer or its production-part policy.
The connector purchasing decision does not change the selected LED or any LED power, data, or level-shifting behavior.
Connector sourceability and minimum-order acceptance do not change connector placement, orientation, alignment, or cable routing.
The source does not identify or alter the interboard power connector type, pin count, pin ordering, pinout, or topology.
The component-purchasing fallback does not affect I2C cable length, speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor policy.
The source does not change the charge-status LED path, connector, resistor, or component-population requirements.
The source does not identify the battery connector or resolve or alter its family, pin count, functions, access, compatibility, or pin-order ambiguity.
